rationale:
structural: The requirement text prescribes two structural obligations: (1) the `OutlineLang` trait method signature `fn search_structure(&self, source: &str, rule: &serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>) -> Result<Vec<Span>, OutlineError>`, and (2) "The default implementation returns an unsupported-language error." A trait method with a different signature, or one that is required rather than defaulted, would break the text. Both obligations are met by the supplied root `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#trait[OutlineLang]/fn[search_structure]`. It has the prescribed signature and a default body returning `Err(unsupported_search(self.name()))`. `fn[unsupported_search]` in the same file builds the selection error "structural search is unsupported for outline language …". It is reached from the root, so it needs no marker. Languages with syntax support override the method through the `language` macro in `outline/languages/mod.rs`. Languages that don't override it, such as plain text, inherit the default, so plain text offers outlining only. The sentence "The operation returns matched byte ranges" describes observable behavior of the overrides and doesn't prescribe a structure. The callers in `sources.rs` only use the capability and need no marker for this requirement.

behavioral: The requirement has two observable obligations. Both have marked tests that assert their outcomes.

1. **A language that supplies the capability returns matched byte ranges within the supplied source.**
   - `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_structural_search_returns_matches_and_rejects_bad_rules_and_source]` runs `languages::Rust.search_structure` on a two-function source with the rule `{"rule":{"kind":"function_item"}}`.
   - It slices the supplied source with each returned `Span` and asserts the results are exactly `["fn first() {}", "fn second() {}"]`. That checks the ranges are byte ranges into the supplied source, and that all matches are returned in order.
   - It also checks that an invalid rule and an unparsable source (`"fn {"`) both return `Err`. The requirement does not spell out those error cases, so this is extra coverage.
   - Only Rust is tested. The requirement describes the trait operation, not per-language behavior, and the bundled languages share one implementation macro. I did not treat the untested languages as a gap.

2. **The default implementation returns an unsupported-language error, and plain text supplies outlining only.**
   - `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[outline_only_languages_report_unsupported_structural_search]` uses `CustomLanguage`. Its `OutlineLang` impl defines only `name`, `extensions`, `outline` and `fingerprint_scheme`, so it uses the trait's default `search_structure`.
   - The test asserts the error message contains "unsupported".
   - It also asserts that `languages::PlainText.search_structure` returns an error whose message contains "plain-text". That confirms plain text offers no structural search.

The trait signature is a structural obligation. It is checked by the tests compiling against it, so it needs no separate behavioral test. `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` is also marked, but it only covers outline behavior and is not needed for this requirement.

I found no unmarked relevant tests and no unacknowledged gaps.
